name: Pravastatin
summary: A hydrophilic statin with minimal CYP-mediated metabolism, used for LDL lowering and cardiovascular risk reduction in primary and secondary prevention.
mechanism: Competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, reducing hepatic cholesterol synthesis and upregulating hepatic LDL receptors to increase LDL clearance.
pharmacodynamics: Lowers LDL-C ~20–30% at standard doses; modest HDL increase and triglyceride reduction.

dosing.adult: 40 mg once daily at bedtime (range 10–80 mg)
dosing.renalAdjustment: Start at 10 mg/day in severe renal impairment

safety.pregnancy: Contraindicated in pregnancy (fetal harm; US FDA category X)
contraindications: Active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevation
monitoring: Liver enzymes at baseline and as indicated

indications: Primary and secondary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular events
clinicalPearls: The least CYP3A4-dependent statin — useful when drug interactions are a concern.
Hydrophilic profile is associated with lower muscle-related adverse effect risk.
good: Patients needing reliable LDL reduction with a low interaction burden.
bad: Not the most potent statin when large LDL reductions are required.
